description: You are a data engineer and you need to ensure that the ETL pipeline can write logs to a specific directory. There is an existing directory at /home/user/etl_logs. Your task is to set the permissions so that only the file owner has read, write, and execute access, and no other users (group or others) have any access at all to this directory. After setting the permissions, list the details (permissions, ownership, etc.) of the directory /home/user/etl_logs in long format and output just this line to a file named /home/user/permissions_check.log. The permissions_check.log should only contain a single line that matches the output of ls -ld /home/user/etl_logs after you have changed the permissions. Make sure not to include any extra lines or explanations in the log file; only include the result of the ls -ld command for the directory.
truth:
Before the task, the directory /home/user/etl_logs must exist and be owned by user user. Example initial permissions could be drwxrwxr-x. The agent is to change permissions to drwx------.

Correct final details:
The directory /home/user/etl_logs should have permissions set to 700 (drwx------), owned by user user and their primary group (typically "user"). The group ownership may be "user" or any default group for the /home/user directory, but must not change from the initial state.

The log file /home/user/permissions_check.log must exist, be readable by the user, and the only line in this file must match the output of:

ls -ld /home/user/etl_logs

Example content (the exact time stamps/number of links may vary):

drwx------ 2 user user 4096 Jun 10 12:34 /home/user/etl_logs

The log file must contain only the output line, without extra content. There should be no trailing blank lines, and the content must reflect the current state after the permissions change.
